# A const whose initializer reads itself, by one hop or by several, is a
# cycle, and the checker refuses it with a position, naming each read on the
# way round.
#
# It used to be accepted by `sngl check`, which never folds, and to take the
# compiler down at `sngl generate`: `evalIdent` reads a const's value by
# evaluating its initializer, so `const a int = a` was evalIdent <-> evalExpr
# until the stack went, with no position and no message. A guard there turned
# that into a page that rendered nothing in silence. The fold keeps the guard
# for IR the checker did not see; a program never reaches it now.

! sngl check selfconst.sngl
stderr 'selfconst.sngl:9:15: a cycle: a reads a; it needs its own value first, so it has none'

! sngl check cycle.sngl
stderr 'cycle.sngl:9:15: a cycle: a reads b, b reads a; each needs the next one''s value first, so none has one'

-- selfconst.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = a

window #home(title="t") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
-- cycle.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = b
const b int = a

window #home(title="t") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
